brief.conference_theme: Environmental and social regeneration: beyond sustainability
brief.panel_theme: Circularity at scale: regenerative sourcing and supply chains

plan.summary: Build a three-person panel on circularity at scale, focusing on regenerative sourcing and supply chains in business. Favor rising or established, budget-conscious candidates with prior conference or presentation experience, and balance sectors, career stages, places, and organization types; national reach allows searches beyond New Haven.
plan.location_focus: National; include New Haven and the Northeast where useful

angles: Business-school and supply-chain researchers studying circular procurement, regenerative agriculture, and scaling reuse
Researchers presenting at circular economy and sustainable business conferences
Corporate sourcing, procurement, and supply-chain leaders implementing circular or regenerative practices
Circular-economy consultants and nonprofit program leaders with practical case studies and conference presentations
State or federal circular-economy, sustainable materials, and responsible-sourcing policy specialists
Think-tank policy experts on producer responsibility and circular supply chains who present to business audiences
Founders of early-stage circular materials, reuse, and regenerative sourcing businesses with demonstrated scale-up work
Small and mid-sized company leaders presenting supply-chain circularity case studies at industry events
Nonprofit and coalition leaders advancing just, regenerative supply chains and circular sourcing
Community or worker-centered advocates connecting materials circularity with equitable sourcing, with public speaking experience
Business or sustainability reporters covering circular supply chains, regenerative sourcing, and materials innovation
Trade-publication editors or podcast hosts who moderate circular economy and sustainable business discussions

cards.name: Aditya Vedantam
cards.job_title: Associate Professor, Operations Management and Strategy; Affiliated Faculty, Center for Supply Chain Analytics
cards.organization: University at Buffalo School of Management
cards.could_speak_on: How business models and operational decisions can move circular supply chains from pilot projects to scale.
talk_ideas: Designing supply-chain contracts for remanufacturing
Circular business models and their environmental trade-offs
Sustainable operations: aligning profitability with environmental performance
cards.bio: Aditya Vedantam is an associate professor in operations management and strategy at the University at Buffalo School of Management, where he is affiliated with the Center for Supply Chain Analytics. His research interests include sustainable operations management, supply-chain management, and new business models for a circular economy.
credentials: PhD, Krannert School of Management, Purdue University
cards.why_fit: Offers a business-school research perspective directly relevant to circular business models, supply-chain design, and scaling more sustainable operations.

past_speaking.event: Talks based on his research to the Institute of Supply Management, Western New York Sustainable Business Roundtable, UB Alumni Association, and Association of Plastic Recyclers

notable_work: Research on revenue-sharing contracts under quality uncertainty in remanufacturing
cards.fit_reason: His current faculty profile confirms direct research fit and multiple prior research talks, including to supply-chain and recycling audiences.

cards.name: Joseph Sarkis
cards.could_speak_on: How circular-economy principles and sustainable supply-chain practices can be embedded across organizations and industries.
talk_ideas: Circular economy strategies for supply-chain management
Environmental sustainability and supply-chain transformation
Using management engineering to connect sustainability goals with operational decisions
cards.bio: Joseph Sarkis is a professor of management in Worcester Polytechnic Institute’s Business School, with an affiliated appointment in Management Engineering. His work includes sustainable supply chains and the circular economy, and he has held a leadership role in a research center focused on transport, technology, circular economy, and sustainable supply chains.
credentials: PhD, Management Sciences, SUNY at Buffalo
cards.why_fit: A senior academic with explicit expertise in circular economy and sustainable supply chains, closely aligned with the panel’s systems-level business focus.
cards.fit_reason: His current WPI profile confirms a strong match on circular economy and sustainable supply chains, along with a documented public podcast appearance.

cards.name: Christopher Marquis
cards.organization: Cambridge Judge Business School, University of Cambridge
cards.could_speak_on: How business accountability and regenerative agriculture connect environmental and social outcomes across value chains.
talk_ideas: Regenerative agriculture and the business value chain
Corporate accountability for social and environmental supply-chain impacts
How business, government, and civil society can support regenerative outcomes
cards.bio: Christopher Marquis is Sinyi Professor of Chinese Management at Cambridge Judge Business School and a Fellow and Director of Studies at Jesus College. His research examines business sustainability, social entrepreneurship, and historical processes; he is the author of *The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs*.
credentials: Author of *The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs*
cards.why_fit: Brings a business-sustainability research lens to regenerative agriculture and supply-chain accountability, with a directly relevant public discussion of regenerative sourcing.

past_speaking.event: Climate Rising podcast: “Regenerative Agriculture and ‘The Profiteers’”

notable_work: The Profiteers: How Business Privatizes Profits and Socializes Costs
Better Business: How the B Corp Movement is Remaking Capitalism

links.label: Climate Rising podcast on regenerative agriculture

cards.fit_reason: Strong connection to regenerative agriculture, business sustainability, and accountability across supply chains, supported by a relevant public podcast appearance.

dropped.name: Nazli Turken
dropped.reason: The supplied Johns Hopkins faculty profile blocked access, and no alternate page was available in this verification pass to confirm her current academic title and role.

cards.name: Deborah Dull
cards.job_title: Founder, Circular Supply Chain Network; Founder, Trillium Digital Services
cards.organization: Circular Supply Chain Network; Trillium Digital Services
cards.could_speak_on: How organizations can operationalize circularity through supply-chain design, inventory practices, and material flows.
talk_ideas: Practical levers for building circular supply chains
Using supply-chain operations to scale circular sourcing and recovery
What organizations can learn from applying circularity across different industries
cards.bio: Deborah Dull is the founder of the Circular Supply Chain Network and Trillium Digital Services. Her supply-chain experience includes work at Microsoft, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and General Electric, and she has authored books on circular supply chains.
credentials: Author of books on circular supply chains
cards.why_fit: Her operational supply-chain focus directly addresses the panel’s question of how circularity can move from ambition to implementation at scale.
cards.fit_reason: Strong direct fit on circular-supply-chain practice, with several public speaking examples and experience across major organizations.

cards.name: Monica Becker
cards.organization: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
cards.could_speak_on: How collaborative product and material initiatives can help businesses embed circularity and safer chemistry across value chains.
talk_ideas: Building cross-sector collaborations to advance circular products
Circularity as a product-design and business strategy challenge
Scaling safer chemistry and materials initiatives across value chains
cards.bio: Monica Becker is Senior Director of Strategy & Development at the Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute, where she leads growth, innovation, and impact initiatives across sectors. Her previous roles include work with the Green Chemistry & Commerce Council and sustainability organizations in academia, government, and consulting.
credentials: Master’s degrees in Civil & Environmental Engineering and Technology & Policy from MIT
B.S. in Engineering from the College of Environmental Science and Forestry
cards.why_fit: She brings practical experience developing industry collaborations across product sectors and value chains, complementing supply-chain operators with a product and materials perspective.
notable_work: Designed and led cross-industry initiatives through the Green Chemistry & Commerce Council, including programs in beauty, personal care, and household products.
cards.fit_reason: Strong cross-sector circularity and product-materials expertise, with a confirmed summit appearance; less specifically focused on supply-chain operations than the top-ranked candidate.

cards.name: Vivian Tai
cards.could_speak_on: How standards-based traceability and better resource visibility can enable circular sourcing and material recovery across supply networks.
talk_ideas: Traceability standards as infrastructure for circular supply chains
Improving material and resource visibility across fragmented value chains
Using cross-industry collaboration to support material recovery
cards.bio: Vivian Tai is identified as Director of Customer Success at GS1 US and works with industries on standards-driven traceability. Her speaker profile describes collaboration with stakeholders to pilot models for resource transparency and material recovery.
cards.why_fit: She can contribute a practical data and standards perspective on the visibility needed to scale circular sourcing and recovery.
cards.fit_reason: Offers a distinct implementation angle—standards and traceability—that connects directly to the information needs of circular supply networks.

cards.name: Anthony Levy
cards.could_speak_on: How circular IT models extend hardware lifecycles, reduce e-waste, and help organizations build more resilient sourcing and supply chains.
talk_ideas: Scaling reuse and refurbishment across enterprise IT supply chains
Measuring embodied carbon and Scope 3 impacts in technology procurement
Business value and practical barriers in extending the life of critical infrastructure
cards.bio: Anthony Levy is Founder and CEO of Circularity First, a group of sustainable IT businesses. The company says it enables organizations to reuse and repurpose technology, and Levy has discussed circular IT and sustainability at business events.
cards.why_fit: Direct founder-operator experience with extending the useful life of technology and putting reuse into organizational practice makes him a close fit for a business panel on circularity at scale.

past_speaking.event: UN Global Compact Network UK 2025 Annual Summit, “Transformative Innovation: How ESG Fuels Competitive Advantage”
COGx, E-Waste World Conference, and SustainX (events named in speaker bio)
Webinar on practical strategies for sustainable IT (November 2024)

notable_work: Circularity First's reuse and repurposing of technology to reduce e-waste and embodied carbon

links.label: UN Global Compact Network UK 2025 speaker page

cards.fit_reason: Strong practitioner-founder match: his company's core work is circular IT reuse, and the evidence includes multiple public speaking appearances.

cards.name: Naomi Davis
cards.could_speak_on: How community-led circular systems can connect regenerative sourcing and waste reuse with local ownership, resilience, and economic wellbeing.
talk_ideas: Building circular neighborhood economies through local ownership and resource reuse
Connecting regenerative sourcing to community wealth and resilience
Designing zero-waste, resource-efficient housing and neighborhood systems
cards.bio: Naomi Davis is the Founder & CEO of Blacks in Green, a nonprofit focused on environmental economic development and community resilience. Its Sustainable Square Mile approach supports community-based economies and systems involving energy, housing, horticulture, tourism, and waste.
cards.why_fit: Offers a community-rooted nonprofit perspective on how circularity and resource systems can support local livelihoods and resilience.
notable_work: Blacks in Green’s Sustainable Square Mile approach
cards.fit_reason: Directly connects community-centered environmental economic development with circular resource systems and has a verified Circularity 24 appearance.

cards.name: Annie Leonard
cards.could_speak_on: How product life-cycle impacts—from sourcing through disposal—shape a just and regenerative circular economy.
talk_ideas: Tracing the environmental and social impacts of products across supply chains
Design justice and zero-waste pathways to a circular economy
Making consumer and business systems accountable for the full life cycle of materials
cards.bio: Annie Leonard is Executive Director of Greenpeace USA and has spent more than two decades investigating and explaining the environmental and social impacts of products. She founded The Story of Stuff Project, which communicates how products are made, used, and discarded.
credentials: Master’s in City and Regional Planning, Cornell University
cards.why_fit: Brings a national advocacy perspective on product life cycles and the environmental and social consequences of sourcing, distribution, and disposal.

past_speaking.event: Design Justice and Zero Waste Conference

notable_work: The Story of Stuff film and project

links.label: Design Justice and Zero Waste Conference

cards.fit_reason: Her documented work on product life cycles and zero-waste advocacy aligns closely with the panel, though the verified speaking appearance is from 2018.

cards.name: Nina Pullman
cards.could_speak_on: What food supply-chain reporting reveals about sourcing impacts, farming practices, and the realities behind sustainability claims.
talk_ideas: Tracing environmental impacts through food supply chains
Small-scale producers and lower-impact sourcing
How journalism can connect consumer choices to supply-chain realities
cards.bio: Nina Pullman is a freelance journalist, producer, and editor specializing in food, supply chains, farming, sustainability, the environment, and travel. Her work includes producing and presenting for BBC Radio 4’s *Farming Today*, producing *The Food Programme*, and founding and editing *Wicked Leeks*.
cards.why_fit: She offers a distinct food-sourcing and reporting perspective, including first-hand coverage of producers and supply chains, complementing business and corporate voices on the panel.
notable_work: Founded and edited *Wicked Leeks*, a magazine for sustainable food and ethical business
Co-produced and co-presented *Who Gives a Fork*, a podcast about stories in popular food supply chains
cards.fit_reason: Strong fit for food sourcing and supply-chain realities; her verified journalism and broadcast experience add a useful communicator perspective.

cards.name: Heather Clancy
cards.could_speak_on: How companies are using business-model innovation and technology to change the business of climate and scale environmental solutions.
talk_ideas: Corporate innovation and climate-focused business models
The role of technology in transforming supply chains
Communicating business climate strategies to a broad audience
cards.bio: Heather Clancy is an award-winning journalist specializing in transformative technology and climate tech. As editor at large for Trellis, formerly GreenBiz, she covers how corporations use business-model innovation and technology in the transition to a low-carbon economy.
credentials: Co-author of *Niche Down: How to Become Legendary By Being Different*
cards.why_fit: Her business-climate reporting is relevant to corporate transformation and scaling solutions, though the verified profile does not establish specific circular-sourcing expertise or past speaking engagements.
cards.fit_reason: Relevant business and climate reporting expertise, but less directly tied to circular supply chains and no past speaking was confirmed.
